stories.title: Komanche, a prominent Spanish-language streamer and Minecraft event organizer, dies at 30
paragraphs: Carlos Mauricio Gómez, known online as Komanche, has died at age 30, according to EL PAÍS and Cadena SER.
The Salvadoran creator was known for Spanish-language streaming and for organizing major Minecraft events, including Squid Craft Games.
Tributes from fellow creators appeared in the collected coverage. The saved reporting does not establish a cause of death.
His death is a major loss for the creator community and the events he helped build.

scoreNotes.general: Multiple Spanish-language news outlets reported the death of a known creator and event organizer on the collection date.
scoreNotes.heat: Coverage across several established outlets and public tributes indicate substantial attention; the saved results provide no audience-wide measurement.
scoreNotes.time: The reports appeared October 26, inside the collection's 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: EL PAÍS and Cadena SER independently report his identity, age, and death. The saved evidence does not establish cause of death, so none is stated.

stories.title: Streamer Awards organizers face a reported threat from Kick streamer BigLoaf
paragraphs: Streamers News reports that Kick streamer BigLoaf threatened in a surfaced video to appear at the 2026 Streamer Awards with weapons and to attack the Twitch community.
The awards are a large creator-led event, making a threat against the gathering a serious safety concern. The saved evidence does not establish that BigLoaf has the means or intent to carry it out.
No organizer, venue, or law-enforcement response was found in the saved results. The report's publication date is not visible in the opened page, so the timing of the development remains uncertain.

scoreNotes.general: A reported threat naming a major creator awards event is consequential and drew attention, but saved evidence is concentrated in one outlet.
scoreNotes.heat: The wording and target attracted online attention; the saved results do not establish the scale of reaction or any official response.
scoreNotes.time: Found during this update's creator research, but the opened report did not show a publication timestamp, so its exact relation to the 24-hour window is uncertain.
scoreNotes.ethos: The source reports a video threat. No independent verification, law-enforcement response, or statement from the awards organizers appears in the saved evidence; it should be treated as a reported threat, not proof of an imminent attack.

nearMisses.reason: A notable change for indie developers, but it was reported October 23 and the saved evidence offers only one article; it ranks below the current creator news. The report says an Enterprise licence will still be required for the relevant runtime, so the change is not cost-free for every developer.

paragraphs: Creative Bloq reports that GameMaker plans to let developers sell games without its current revenue share from 2027.
The saved article also says developers will still need an Enterprise licence for the applicable runtime, so the announcement does not mean every use of GameMaker becomes free.
